ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Why younger children are susceptible

A clinician reviews several cases of retropharyngeal abscess occurring after upper respiratory infections in children younger than 5 years. Similar infections are less frequent in older children. Which age-related feature best explains this distribution?

  1. Regression of retropharyngeal lymph nodes with age
  2. Progressive enlargement of the palatine tonsillar crypts
  3. Age-related widening of the eustachian tubes
  4. Increasing acidity of gastric contents with age
  5. Reduced salivary secretion in older children
Answer and explanation

Regression of retropharyngeal lymph nodes with age

Retropharyngeal nodes drain nearby upper-airway structures in young children and regress as children grow.

Option explanations

Regression of retropharyngeal lymph nodes with age: Retropharyngeal nodes drain nearby upper-airway structures in young children and regress as children grow.

Progressive enlargement of the palatine tonsillar crypts: This does not explain the particular early-childhood susceptibility to infection of retropharyngeal nodes.

Age-related widening of the eustachian tubes: This relates more directly to middle-ear ventilation than to suppuration of retropharyngeal lymph nodes.

Increasing acidity of gastric contents with age: Gastric acidity does not explain the distribution of these postinfectious neck abscesses.

Reduced salivary secretion in older children: This is not the normal developmental mechanism behind the age pattern.
